title: Aim
intro: The target is off the straight line. Drag the arrow head to aim the packet, watch the preview curve, then play and observe at the peak.
goal: Drag the arrow head to aim at the target, then Play and Observe at the peak.

tutorial.title: Aim
tutorial.text: The target is up and to the right. Drag the white dot at the tip of the arrow to aim the packet.
tutorial.phys: The arrow is the momentum k₀. Its direction is where the packet goes; its length is how fast.

tutorial.title: Preview
tutorial.text: The faint curve updates as you aim: it previews PT(t) for your setup. Aim until it peaks high, then press Play and Observe at the peak.

tutorial.title: The long version
tutorial.text: Every level has a one-line physics point here. Why? opens the full explanation. That is the end of the tutorial: Chapter 1 starts with real puzzles.

physics.point: Momentum sets where the packet goes. In free space its centre moves in a straight line at velocity k₀ (ħ = m = 1).

idea: The arrow is the packet's average momentum. A plane wave exp(i k·r) has its wavefronts perpendicular to k, and the packet travels along k.
The centre of a free packet moves like a classical particle, in a straight line at constant speed (Ehrenfest's theorem). Only its width behaves quantum mechanically, spreading as it goes.
maths: The target centre is at (29, 13) and the packet starts at (8, 31): a displacement of (21, −18), so the direction is atan2(−18, 21) = −40.6°, with y pointing down the screen.
The meter peaks at t ≈ 12.2, slightly before the centre arrives, because the spreading packet starts filling the target early. The best P<sub>T</sub> is 33%.
try: Aim 10° too high or too low and watch the preview peak drop: the packet is about 5 units wide on arrival, the target 7.
Leave the arrow flat (0°) and play: P<sub>T</sub> stays at zero.
